x: We are badly in need of a few first class sprinters for our senior matches as Lionel Grimshaw had muscle trouble and Gordon Lowers was not always available.

Mike Broadbent and Gordon Lowers were first two home in the 100 yards, while Jim Beaumont and Heathfield were second and third in the 440. John Cope won the 880 yards with Archie Bedford third and Len Marchant won the mile with Len Adams third.

This was held at Tooting and in the senior match Gordon Lowers won the 100 yards in 10.6 secs. and John Cope won the 440 in 52.7 secs. Cope also turned out in the 220 and gained a point by filling fourth place.

In the circumstances, and seeing it is yet early in the season, I think we did quite well in being placed 4th of the competing clubs. The 100 yards saw us with two competitors in the final, which was quite a good start, and Gordon Lowers finished third with R.

In the Senior 4 x 110 yds. we had Mike Broadbent, Gordon Lowers, Basil Walden and Jimmy Rae running for us and although we had the lead at the last change-over, Rae had to give best to Clay Gibbs, the coloured
Merrett for 3rd place with Gordon Lowers close behind them. Basil also gained 3rd place in the 220 yards final and so managed to split the three Herne Hill runners.
In the 100 yards we had Gordon Lowers and Basil Walden, and they both ran well to finish 2nd and 3rd in a race won in 10 seconds dead by Grieve of S.L.H.
Points for the Junior match were: Belgrave H. 26; South London H. 19. In the Senior events Gordon Lowers won the 100 yards and Alan Sexton, home on leave from the R.A.F., won the 220 yards.
In the 100 yards we had first two places through Gordon Lowers and Basil Walden, and the latter also won the 220 yards with Alan Picton in second place.

The 100 yards saw Basil Walden and Gordon Lowers in front and Basil also won the 220 with Alan Picton in third place. Ches Walker won the 880 and Bob Taylor filled fourth place to score a point for us, but in the 440 yards Herne Hill had the first three home with Jim Heathfield first of our runners.

This was held on the same evening as the Tadworth match and our numbers suffered accordingly, but we did not do so badly, and in a five-sided contest we finished in third position. Gordon Lowers won the 100 yards and Mullen won the 220, while Stan Davies was third in the Mile and Bergvalds was second in the Shot Putt.

Gordon Lowers gave us a good start by winning the 100 yards, with Dicky Barlett in fifth place. Basil Walden won the 220 yards with " Ginger " Holtum in third place and then Alan Picton won the 440, beating Ede of Epsom, the international runner.
A triangular match was held at Tooting on August 2nd between S.L.H., Surrey A.C. and ourselves. Gordon Lowers once again won the 100, beating such men as Grieve, of S.L.H., and D.

There were, however, three field events and from these Herne Hill scored 10, Sutton and Cheam 7, and ourselves 2, which shows where the weakness in the club lies. Gordon Lowers won the 100 in 10.3 secs. on grass, and D.
Gordon Lowers retained his 100 yards title in the good time of 10.6 secs, on a very heavy track, and then Ches Walker won the 1 mile in 4 mins. 28.8 secs. with Bob Taylor in second place.
" Ginger " Holtum won the 100 yards and was also third in the 220, while Gordon Lowers made a welcome appearance to gain second place in the 100.

Gordon Lowers ran second in the 100 yards, with Eric Bishop gaining third place in the 440 yards. In the middle-distance events we did better, with Ian Badiali winning the quarter, Jack Brown the half-mile and Bill Lucas the mile, a very creditable trio of wins.

Goodchild, a fairly new member, with Ian Forrester second and Gordon Lowers third. Alan Picton won the 600 yards with Maurice Jones second and Eddie Lacey third, while Arthur Bruce won the 3 miles run, with Archie Bedford second and Ken Stimpson third.
